title: Can the Six Traditional Tamil Flavors of Arusuvai Be Represented Computationally? A Six-Dimensional Framework for Food-Related Oral Chemosensation
content: Sensory data are difficult to compare when attribute definitions, acquisition protocols or missing measurements differ. The Arusuvai Computational Taste Framework (ACTF) formalizes six Tamil oral sensory descriptors as named, normalized coordinates with explicit provenance and protocol metadata. A versioned JSON schema and Python implementation distinguish absent ratings from measured zero, reject incompatible protocol declarations, and compute exact geometric completion bounds for incomplete profiles. Eight constructed profiles round-tripped without information loss; 28 complete distances agreed with a separately written JavaScript implementation within 1.2 × 10−16. Across 1,764 synthetic common-mask comparisons, every reference distance lay within its calculated bounds. Removing pungency and astringency produced 36 strict ordering reversals among 168 candidate-order comparisons under zero filling; both orderings were feasible for every comparison under the completion box. A secondary analysis of four published food-cluster means mapped four measured taste attributes into ACTF while retaining pungency and astringency as missing and savouriness outside the six-coordinate schema. All six resulting conditional distance intervals overlapped. This example highlights why an apparently precise partial profile need not support a full-profile ranking. ACTF contributes an inspectable, culturally indexed data contract and conservative comparison workflow, not a new biological taxonomy or validated model of human similarity. Prospective bilingual and psychophysical studies are specified to evaluate construct validity and practical utility.
